name: How are shower walls and floors waterproofed before tiling?

mainEntity.name: How are shower walls and floors waterproofed before tiling?

acceptedAnswer.text: Proper waterproofing is the most critical stage of shower construction because tile and grout are water-resistant, not waterproof. Before placing a single tile, installers construct a sloped shower pan to direct moisture toward the drain weep holes and attach moisture-resistant backer board to the walls. Installers then apply continuous waterproofing—either a sheet membrane or multiple coats of liquid waterproofing—over all seams, screw heads, and corners. In the Denver metro area, seasonal shifts and dry indoor air can cause minor framing movement, making a flexible, properly sealed membrane critical to prevent leaks from reaching subflooring or adjacent finished spaces.
acceptedAnswer.description: Crews install moisture-resistant backer board and apply a seamless sheet or liquid waterproof membrane across all walls, seams, and the sloped shower pan.
